To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have isolated cDNA clones for the major whey protein and caseins from rabbit mammary glands and that the nucleotide sequences of the cDNA clones are currently being determined.
we identified the four major milk protein mRNAs and their corresponding translation products, and we constructed cDNA clones for rabbit alpha- and kappa-casein and alpha-lacalbumin.

(i) we have isolated and characterized cDNA clones for rabbit caseins and for alpha-lactalbumins, which will be useful in future studies on the structure and expression of these genes; and (ii) the major mRNA species of the rabbit mammary gland, identified by hybridization of cytoplasmic RNA with the cDNA clones, correspond to those previously identified by in vitro translation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of cDNA clones representing the major mRNA species of the lactating mammary gland of the rabbit.
the isolation of complementary DNA sequences for major milk proteins from lactating rabbit glands and the construction of bacterial recomblants containing casein cDNA sequences.
the characterization of the major protein-encoding mRNAs of rabbit lactating mammar glands, and we present the first cDNA clones of rabbit caseins and of alpha-lactalbumins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the major proteins synthesized in the mammary gland are caseins and alpha- lactalbumin.

(i) the major mRNA species of lactating mammary gland range from 0.5 to 5.0 kilobases in size, (ii) the four major proteins synthesized in vitro correspond to alpha-lactalbumi, x-, kappa-, and alpha-caseins and (iii) the four major mRNA species are represented by alpha-lactalbumina and x-, kappa-,and alpha-casein cDNA sequences.
the cDNA clones for the major milk proteins of the lactating rabbit are available and have been characterized in terms of their nucleotide and protein sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have cloned the major casein and alpha- lactalbumin mRNA species from rabbit mammary glands, and have shown that these cDNA clones can be used to identify the corresponding mRNA species in total cytoplasmic RNA from lactating mammary tissue.
the cDNA clones for the major caseins and alpha lactalbumin were identified and characterized.
we have identified and partially characterized four major caseins and one whey protein (alpha-lactalbumin), which are the major translation products from rabbit lactating gland polyadenylated mRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed an efficient procedure for the isolation of cDNA clones from the major mRNA species of rabbit mammary glands.
the major milk proteins of rabbit can be synthesized in vitro by translation of mRNA from lactating rabbit milk glands.
the major milk proteins of rabbit are encoded by mRNAs with sizes ranging between 1.0 and 2.5 kb, and that the corresponding cDNA clones have been isolated and characterized.
